name: Bouncing Betty
slug: The Twin Peaks inn and tavern Gerk aims at for a doorway, also called Bouncing Benny's.
description: Inn and tavern in Twin Peaks, also heard as Bouncing Benny's. The front door opens onto a busy street, and the upstairs is the sleeping area; one account gives the inn a third floor, and the rooms have been moved since the party last knew the layout. They have slept there in game, though not recently—the last stop was before the long boat trip toward Lake Nyx, around the time they collected Plymouth. The barn was rebuilt. From its second story you look down on stables and a wagon set in the center, and Gerk has slept there more than once. An old sideline ended in that barn when a wayward bard and a drunk wizard killed a mule or donkey with a levitation spell, left the body, and the party made some gold.

log.summary: Gerk chooses this Twin Peaks tavern as his doorway target and aims for the upstairs hallway in front of the rooms, because the front door opens onto a busy street. The party argues the name and whether this building or another local tavern has the large stage they remember. Sylan says the rooms have been moved since they were last familiar with the layout. Confusion then shifts Gerk's doorway from the upstairs hall to the barn loft, about twenty feet off.
